title: "MP4 or WebM? Choosing a Format for Your Presentation Video" (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: MP4 or WebM? Choosing Your Video Format
slides.notes: You've turned your deck into a video. Now, which file format should it be? MP4 and WebM are both good, and here's how to choose.

slides.title: A video file has two layers
bullets: Container: the file type, like .mp4 or .webm
Codecs: how video and audio are compressed
What matters: can the destination play it?
slides.notes: Every video file has a container, like dot mp4, wrapping compressed video and audio. You don't need codec names. Just ask whether the destination can play it.

slides.title: MP4 is most portable; WebM suits the web
bullets: MP4: phones, computers, TVs, most platforms
WebM on phones and TVs: varies
slides.notes: MP4 plays almost everywhere, so it's the safest bet for uploads. WebM is a solid web format, but sometimes needs converting for a specific destination.

slides.title: Work backwards from where it's going
bullets: Your own website: WebM or MP4
YouTube, social, LMS: check accepted formats
slides.notes: Start with the destination. Either format works on your own website. For email, shared drives or an uncertain LMS, MP4 is the safe choice.

slides.title: One video, three destinations
bullets: LMS: MP4 only, so convert once
slides.notes: Take a five-minute product overview saved as WebM. Embed it on your site, upload to YouTube, and convert once for the LMS. Then watch it through to check sync.

slides.title: Ordinary deck in, MP4 or WebM out
bullets: Try Basic first, no subscription needed
slides.notes: On Pro, a.i. directs your video, tightening the story and timing each scene to your narration. Try Basic first, and get an MP4 or WebM at powerpoint2vid.com.
